uncited: This family distinguishes itself from siblings like [Two-Pass Shadow Casting (Kajiya and Von Herzen)](2196-two-pass-shadow-casting-kajiya-and-von-herzen.md) by focusing on local shading rather than global shadow computation, and from [Path Tracing and Sampling](2526-path-tracing-and-sampling.md) by using deterministic or semi-analytical approximations instead of stochastic integration.

The core mechanism involves computing a surface normal approximation from the volume data gradient $\mathbf{g} = \nabla V$ and applying a local illumination model (e.g., Phong, Lambertian, or microfacet-based) to determine the color contribution of a light source.
**Gradient Estimation:** The normal $\mathbf{n}$ is approximated by normalizing the gradient vector $\mathbf{g}$ at the intersection point or voxel center.
A variant where directional lights illuminate both front and back faces.
